body:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: *New incident* opened by @Wei Chen
Severity: SEV-4 (minor)
Service: Docs site (release notes)
Summary: Public release notes page briefly published with incomplete content (missing sections / partial template render)
Start: now

Wei Chen: Seeing a weird release notes page live on docs. It’s the new model release note generated from changelog artifacts, but the body is basically just the header + category bullets. No “What changed” text, no links. Looks like an incomplete render.

Elliot Price: Can you drop the URL + build SHA? Also was this in the RSS/JSON feed too?

Wei Chen: URL: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/release-notes/models/2025-04-02/ (don’t think we should share broadly). Build: redwood-docs deploy #23811. It’s also in the RSS feed as a blank-ish entry.

Incident Bot: Acknowledged by @Elliot Price

Connor O'Brien: Quick gut check: is this coming from the changelog generator artifact or the docs build rendering step?

Wei Chen: I pulled the generated artifact from the build logs and it’s missing `public.summary` and `public.details`. The template renders the header regardless, so it published an “empty” page.

Sahana Iyer: That sounds like the artifact was generated with required fields missing but our docs build didn’t fail hard. We added validation in CI for registry changes, but the docs repo pipeline might not be enforcing “non-empty” content.

Jada Williams: Any chance this was an embargoed/internal-only note and the redaction pass nulled out the public fields?

Wei Chen: It’s not embargoed. It looks like the generator got a change event but didn’t attach the human-authored release note entry. So it created a shell.

Chloe Martin: If it ingested a `model_version_promoted` event without a corresponding metadata delta / `release_note_entry`, it might still emit a stub.

Dylan Brooks: Mitigation: can we immediately roll back that docs deploy + purge CDN cache? Even if it’s minor, customers seeing a blank note looks bad.

Elliot Price: Doing that now. I’m going to redeploy from previous successful build and invalidate the release-notes path.

Connor O'Brien: +1 rollback. Also we should stop the pipeline from publishing if the artifact is missing required public fields. We already have a check in the registry repo (PR-18452-ish), but this is docs build consumption.

Sahana Iyer: I can add a guard in the docs build step: fail if any changelog entry has empty `title`/`summary`/`details` for public entries OR if it’s tagged `public=true` and has zero content.

Wei Chen: Confirming impact window: page was live for ~6-8 minutes. I saw it at 10:07, first deploy log line at 10:00-ish. Hard to know if anyone hit it.

Incident Bot: Status update requested: impact, mitigation, next steps

Elliot Price: Mitigation in progress: rolling back to deploy #23807 and purging CDN cache for `/release-notes/models/*`.

Elliot Price: Rollback complete. I’m no longer seeing the incomplete page; RSS entry also gone after cache purge.

Marissa Cole: Thanks. Please make sure this doesn’t become “release notes are unreliable” with enterprise folks. Can we add a quick note to the internal launch thread + track as a follow-up ticket?

Connor O'Brien: Root cause hypothesis: generator emitted an entry on promotion event without a validated public note payload. Docs build happily rendered it.
Action items:
1) Generator: don’t emit `public=true` entries unless required fields are present OR mark as `draft=true` and docs build should skip.
2) Docs build: add hard failure + skip drafts.
3) Monitoring: add a canary check that fetches latest release note page and asserts non-empty sections.

Chloe Martin: I’ll take (1) on the generator side. We should treat promotion-only events as internal audit entries unless there’s an attached public note block.

Sahana Iyer: I’ll take (2). Will patch redwood-docs pipeline today and add a unit test fixture with missing fields.

Wei Chen: I’ll take (3) and update the docs playbook with “rollback/purge steps” + “what to check” before publishing.

Elliot Price: For postmortem-lite:
- Customer impact: low, short window, no known customer report
- Data exposure: none
- Fix: rollback + cache purge
- Prevent: validation + draft semantics

Incident Bot: Incident marked as *Mitigated* by @Elliot Price

Dylan Brooks: Also please ensure the Console release notes feed wouldn’t show this kind of stub. If the internal API returns empty notes, Console should hide/label as draft.

Jada Williams: Good call. I’ll add a quick check on the Console side to not render public feed items with empty `summary/details` (and log an error). Will file a follow-up.

Marissa Cole: Add the follow-ups to the launch checklist (CI gates + publishing rules). Let’s keep wording consistent with the taxonomy/style guide too.

Connor O'Brien: I’ll open an ENG release follow-up to ensure the “release note preview” check is required across repos, not just registry. This slipped through because docs deploy path bypassed the normal PR validation.

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: Incident closed. Please link follow-up tickets in the incident channel topic or in the retro doc.
